title: GB1: do interaction terms help outside the training neighborhood?
attribution: New AI-assisted public technical study for this profile. Not prior Jackie Ng research or the private AtomBios model.
task: Predict log1p experimental GB1 IgG-Fc binding fitness for four-site variants, not delivery, stability alone or protein generation.
license: Original article/data: CC BY 4.0; cite Wu et al. (2016), eLife 5:e16965. Mirror adds split and sequence columns; this study uses original Variants and Fitness fields only.
split: Custom mutation-distance extrapolation: 0–2 training, 3 validation, 4 test. All finite nonnegative original Fitness rows; no FLIP keep filter. Not an official FLIP leaderboard result.
selection: Alpha selected on validation RMSE from fixed grid; no refit on validation, test never used for selection.
limitations: Four mutable sites in one protein; not a general protein model.
Sequence-only additive/pairwise model; no structure-derived features or coordinates.
Assay fitness is a selection/enrichment outcome; not pure binding affinity or stability.
Related variants share a scaffold and residue states across splits; disjoint variants are not disjoint proteins.
All retained source rows include low/zero fitness observations and uneven counts; no replicate uncertainty or count weighting model.
Ridge pairwise terms cannot represent higher-order interactions.
No therapeutic, BBB or drug-delivery validation. Predictions may be negative on the log scale; they are unconstrained regression outputs, not physical values.
